record.summary: An explanatory notice and template adopted by the Commission for the public summary of training content that providers of general-purpose AI models must publish under Article 53(1)(d) of the AI Act, where using the template is mandatory. It sets a common minimal baseline in three sections: general information on the model and its training content, a list of data sources such as public and private datasets, scraped online data, user data and synthetic data, and data processing aspects relevant to rights such as copyright. The summary helps parties with legitimate interests, including copyright holders, exercise their rights under Union law.
record.notes: Published on 24 July 2025. The notice and template are published in all 24 official EU languages, and the template is also offered in English as an editable document for providers to complete. Providers must also disclose, among other things, the top 10% of internet domains scraped (top 5% or 1,000 domains for SMEs), and update the summary every six months or sooner when further training requires a materially significant update. The obligation applies from 2 August 2025, and by 2 August 2027 for models placed on the market before that date; failure to publish can lead to enforcement by the AI Office from 2 August 2026, with fines of up to 3% of annual worldwide turnover or EUR 15 million, whichever is higher. The template complements the guidelines for providers of general-purpose AI models and the General-Purpose AI Code of Practice. The Commission's page for the notice and template shows a last update of 26 March 2026.

verification.note: Re-read in the recheck of 17 Oct 2026: the Commission library page (official, stored 11 Oct 2026) confirms the title, publication on 24 July 2025, the template's aim, the 24 language versions and a last update of 26 March 2026. Stored in this run: the Commission's Q&A on the template (last update 26 March 2026; proposed as secondary_url), which states that using the template is mandatory under Article 53(1)(d) and describes its sections, the copyright purpose, updating and enforcement; and the Commission's press release of 24 July 2025, which says the Commission adopted the template and that it assists copyright holders. The notice and template themselves are offered only through ec.europa.eu/newsroom/dae/, which ec.europa.eu's robots.txt disallows, so they are not stored. Version 1's statements that the template is required under Article 53(1)(d) of the AI Act and supports the exercise of copyright and other rights are not shown in the library page; the Q&A and the press release state them.

title.quote: Explanatory Notice and Template for the Public Summary of Training Content for general-purpose AI models
1 - Explanatory Notice and Template for the Public Summary of Training Content for general-purpose AI models - English (PDF)

date_published.quote: PRESS RELEASE Publication 24 July 2025 The Commission has published a template to help General-Purpose AI (GPAI) providers summarise the content used to train their model.

status.quote: The Template annexed to this Explanatory Notice aims to provide a common minimal baseline for the information to be made publicly available in the Summary of Training Content for general-purpose AI models.
Below, you can download the template and the explanatory note in all EU 24 official languages.

summary.quote: “Today’s template adopted by the Commission is another important step towards trustworthy and transparent AI.

summary.locator: How do these guidelines and the template support providers
summary.quote: Under Article 53(1)(d) of the AI Act, using the Template is mandatory.

summary.locator: Who is expected to publish a summary
summary.quote: Any provider of general-purpose AI models, including those with systemic risks, that places such models on the Union market is required to publish respective summaries.

The Template annexed to this Explanatory Notice aims to provide a common minimal baseline for the information to be made publicly available in the Summary of Training Content for general-purpose AI models.

summary.locator: What type of information should the summary contain?
summary.quote: The Template provides a uniform baseline for information to be publicly disclosed in the Summary, consisting of three main sections:

summary.locator: What type of information should the summary contain?
summary.quote: such as publicly available datasets, private datasets, data scraped from online sources, user data and synthetic data

summary.locator: What type of information should the summary contain?
summary.quote: This section requires information on certain data processing aspects important for exercising the rights of parties with legitimate interests under Union law, such as copyright
This template will also assist parties with legitimate interests, such as copyright holders, in exercising their rights under Union law.
2 - Template for the Public Summary of Training Content for General-Purpose AI models - English (DOC)

notes.quote: Below, you can download the template and the explanatory note in all EU 24 official languages.
2 - Template for the Public Summary of Training Content for General-Purpose AI models - English (DOC)

notes.locator: How are copyright and intellectual property rights addressed?
notes.quote: a list the top 10% of all domains that have been scraped from the internet (for SMEs top 5% or 1000, whichever is lower)
The Summary should be updated at six-month intervals, or sooner if the new data used for further training requires a materially significant update of the content of the Summary

notes.locator: When will the obligation for the public summary start to apply?
notes.quote: The obligation to publish the summary becomes applicable as of 2 August 2025. For models placed on the market before this date, providers should take the necessary steps to make the corresponding summaries available no later than 2 August 2027.

notes.locator: What are the consequences if a provider fails to publish a summary?
notes.quote: Failure to provide this summary can lead to enforcement actions by the AI Office as of 2 August 2026. Non-compliance may result in fines of up to 3% of the provider's annual total worldwide turnover in the preceding financial year, or 15 000 000 Euros, whichever is higher.
It complements the guidelines on the scope of the rules for general-purpose AI models, published 18 July, and the General-Purpose AI Code of Practice released on 10 July.
